items.prompt: What is the outermost layer of the Earth called?

options.label: Crust
options.feedback: Correct. The crust is the thin, solid outer shell of the Earth, the layer we live on.

options.label: Mantle
options.feedback: The mantle lies below the crust, not on top. The crust is the outermost layer.

options.label: Core
options.feedback: The core is the innermost layer, far below the crust.

options.label: Lithosphere
options.feedback: The lithosphere is a rigid shell that includes the crust and the top of the mantle, but it is not the name for the outer layer alone.

items.ok_line: The crust is the Earth's solid outer shell.
items.ko_line: Remember the order: crust is outside, mantle and core are deeper.
items.exp_text: The crust is the Earth's outermost layer, a thin solid shell of rock. It is the part we stand on and the thinnest of the three main layers: crust, mantle, and core.

items.prompt: Which layer of the Earth is the thickest?

options.label: Crust
options.feedback: The crust is very thin compared to the other layers, so it cannot be the thickest.

options.label: Mantle
options.feedback: Correct. The mantle is about 2,900 kilometers thick and makes up most of Earth's volume.

options.label: Outer core
options.feedback: The outer core is deep but its thickness is only about 2,200 kilometers, less than the mantle.

options.label: Inner core
options.feedback: The inner core is the smallest layer, with a radius of about 1,200 kilometers.

items.ok_line: The mantle is the thickest layer of the Earth.
items.ko_line: Remember the mantle is by far the thickest single layer.
items.exp_text: The mantle is the thickest layer of the Earth, extending from below the crust down to the core. It is made of solid rock that can slowly flow over long periods.

items.prompt: What is the Earth's inner core made of?

options.label: Liquid rock (magma)
options.feedback: Magma is melted rock, not the material of the inner core. The inner core is solid metal.

options.label: Solid rock
options.feedback: The inner core is not made of rock; it is made mostly of iron and nickel in solid form.

options.label: Solid iron and nickel
options.feedback: Correct. The inner core is a solid ball of iron and nickel, held solid by enormous pressure.

options.label: Liquid iron and nickel
options.feedback: Liquid iron and nickel make up the outer core, not the inner core.

items.ok_line: The inner core is solid iron and nickel.
items.ko_line: Remember the inner core is solid metal, unlike the liquid outer core.
items.exp_text: The inner core is a solid sphere of iron and nickel. Even though temperatures are extremely high, the pressure is so immense that the metal stays solid.

items.prompt: Which layer of the Earth is liquid?

options.label: Crust
options.feedback: The crust is solid rock; it is not liquid.

options.label: Mantle
options.feedback: The mantle is solid rock that can flow very slowly, but it is not liquid like water.

options.label: Inner core
options.feedback: The inner core is solid, not liquid.

options.label: Outer core
options.feedback: Correct. The outer core is a layer of liquid iron and nickel surrounding the solid inner core.

items.ok_line: The outer core is the only liquid layer of the Earth.
items.ko_line: Remember the outer core is liquid metal; the other layers are solid.
items.exp_text: The outer core is a layer of liquid iron and nickel. It lies between the mantle and the solid inner core, and its movement generates Earth's magnetic field.

items.prompt: What is the main chemical element found in Earth's core?

options.label: Iron
options.feedback: Correct. Iron is the dominant element in both the inner and outer core, along with some nickel.

options.label: Oxygen
options.feedback: Oxygen is abundant in the crust and mantle, but not the main element of the core.

options.label: Silicon
options.feedback: Silicon is common in the crust and mantle, but the core is mostly iron.

options.label: Carbon
options.feedback: Carbon is not the main element; it is rare in the core compared to iron.

items.ok_line: Iron is the main element in Earth's core.
items.ko_line: Remember iron and nickel are the core's metals, not oxygen or silicon.
items.exp_text: Iron makes up most of Earth's core, with some nickel. This heavy metal sank to the center when the early Earth was molten, forming the dense core.

items.prompt: What is the layer just below the crust called?

options.label: Outer core
options.feedback: The outer core is much deeper, far below the mantle. The layer right under the crust is the mantle.

options.label: Mantle
options.feedback: Correct. The mantle is the thick layer of rock directly beneath the crust.

options.label: Inner core
options.feedback: The inner core is at the very center, not just below the crust.

options.label: Asthenosphere
options.feedback: The asthenosphere is a weak part of the upper mantle, not a separate layer above the mantle.

items.ok_line: The mantle is right below the crust.
items.ko_line: Remember the order: crust, mantle, outer core, inner core.
items.exp_text: The mantle lies directly below the crust and extends down to the outer core. It is made of hot, solid rock that can slowly convect.

items.prompt: How deep is the deepest part of Earth's crust under the oceans?

options.label: About 5 kilometers
options.feedback: That is close to the average depth of ocean crust, but not the thickest part; the deepest ocean crust is about 10 kilometers thick.

options.label: About 70 kilometers
options.feedback: That thickness is typical of continental crust, not oceanic crust.

options.label: About 10 kilometers
options.feedback: Correct. Oceanic crust is thin, averaging about 7 kilometers but reaching about 10 kilometers in places.

options.label: About 100 kilometers
options.feedback: That depth is far too deep for any crust; the mantle starts much shallower under oceans.

items.ok_line: Oceanic crust is roughly 10 kilometers thick at most.
items.ko_line: Remember oceanic crust is thin compared to continental crust.
items.exp_text: Oceanic crust is thinner than continental crust, usually about 7 kilometers thick and at most around 10 kilometers. It is made of denser rock like basalt.

items.prompt: How thick is the continental crust on average?

options.label: About 5 kilometers
options.feedback: That is too thin for continental crust; it is more typical of oceanic crust.

options.label: About 10 kilometers
options.feedback: That is roughly the maximum for oceanic crust, not the average for continents.

options.label: About 30 kilometers
options.feedback: That is close, but the average is a bit more; many sources say about 35 kilometers.

options.label: About 35 kilometers
options.feedback: Correct. Continental crust averages about 35 kilometers thick, though it can be thicker under mountain ranges.

items.ko_line: Remember continents are thicker than the ocean floor, not thinner.
items.exp_text: Continental crust averages about 35 kilometers in thickness. It is thicker and less dense than oceanic crust, which is why continents stand higher.

items.prompt: What is the name of the boundary between the crust and the mantle?

options.label: Mohorovičić discontinuity
options.feedback: Correct. This boundary, often called the Moho, separates the crust from the mantle.

options.label: Asthenosphere
options.feedback: The asthenosphere is a zone within the upper mantle, not a boundary between layers.

options.label: Lithosphere
options.feedback: The lithosphere is the rigid outer shell that includes the crust and part of the mantle, not the boundary itself.

options.label: Gutenberg discontinuity
options.feedback: That is the boundary between the mantle and the outer core, not between crust and mantle.

items.ok_line: The Moho is the crust-mantle boundary.
items.ko_line: Remember the Moho is crust-to-mantle; the Gutenberg is mantle-to-core.
items.exp_text: The Mohorovičić discontinuity, or Moho, is the sharp boundary where rock composition changes from crust to mantle. It was discovered by studying earthquake waves.

items.prompt: What is the boundary between the mantle and the outer core called?

options.label: Mohorovičić discontinuity
options.feedback: That is the crust-mantle boundary, not the mantle-core boundary.

options.label: Gutenberg discontinuity
options.feedback: Correct. The Gutenberg discontinuity is the boundary between the solid mantle and the liquid outer core.

options.label: Lithosphere
options.feedback: The lithosphere is a rigid shell near the surface, not a boundary deep inside.

options.label: Upper-lower mantle boundary
options.feedback: That is a boundary within the mantle, not between mantle and core.

items.ok_line: The Gutenberg separates mantle from outer core.
items.ko_line: Remember the Gutenberg is deep; the Moho is shallow.
items.exp_text: The Gutenberg discontinuity marks the base of the mantle, where solid rock gives way to the liquid iron of the outer core. It is located about 2,900 kilometers deep.
